title: MadEvolve: Evolutionary Optimization of Cosmological Algorithms with Large Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary optimization of cosmological reconstruction and prediction algorithms with tunable code and physics-based simulation metrics
mechanism.populationDetail: The program database combines a three-descriptor MAP-Elites grid with five semi-isolated island subpopulations connected by fixed-interval ring migration; the grid archive is distinct from the island organization.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The system maintains a MAP-Elites quality-diversity archive with one fitness-best program per complexity/diversity/performance cell, plus a fixed-capacity global multi-elite archive containing top programs by fitness.
mechanism.replacementDetail: At every five generations, 10% of each island's best members migrate to a neighbor in a ring; island elitism is not enforced, while MAP-Elites cells and the global elite archive apply separate elitist admission rules.
mechanism.generationDetail: The ensemble supports localized differential patches, complete full rewrites for broad exploration, and synthesis that combines ideas from multiple reference programs; mode usage varies across these operators.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Prompts include parent performance metrics and areas for improvement. Task evaluators expose decomposed per-scale or per-simulation measurements; the task-specific scalar fitness may include a penalty (e.g. BAO combined score). MAP-Elites uses complexity and embedding-diversity as archive descriptors, not competing objective scores.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The main parent is sampled from the population with a stated balance toward high-fitness solutions; inspiration retrieval separately draws the global best, recent top performers, and structurally diverse MAP-Elites neighbors. Exact focal-parent sampling probabilities are not specified, and synthesis can use multiple reference programs as true sources.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Every candidate's numerical algorithm parameters are separately optimized by a budgeted derivative-free or autodiff/Adam inner loop before fitness is recorded; this nested program-structure/continuous-parameter optimization is not directly represented by the Chapters 3-7 mechanism labels.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/MadEvolve Evolutionary Optimization of Cosmological Algorithms with Large Language Models.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey already cites MadEvolve for islands/migration, QD and multi-elite archives, fixed generation modes, adaptive model selection, approximate evaluation, and scalar objective search. Its current explore-exploit subsection emphasizes fixed diff/rewrite ratios but should also account for UCB1 adaptive model routing. Generation-mode and model-selection controllers are separate. Synthesis is available but its default weight is unspecified.
